designs.title: Fanad Head Lighthouse
designs.why: Solid poster structure and accurate facts (1817, 1886, 22 m), but the engraving reads as an auto-trace up close: blobby double contours on the cliffs and cottages, and the bottom third is a near-solid mass of ink that becomes a heavy, stiff patch on a $50 tee. The ends of the arched FANAD HEAD drop past the LIGHTHOUSE rule and crowd it. From 3 m it reads as a framed gift-shop souvenir, not as apparel.
designs.fix: Redraw or clean the line art with real engraved hatching, and open up the lower foreground (lighter rocks, more paper showing) so the print breathes and drapes.

designs.title: Portland Head Light
designs.why: Best composition of the set: the keeper's house and tower sit as a strong diagonal and the fence line gives depth. Fact panel is tidy. The same traced, mushy line quality and a dense, nearly solid bottom third weigh it down, and the outer letters of the arched PORTLAND HEAD crowd the LIGHT subtitle rule.
designs.fix: Thin the foreground rocks and surf to about half the ink coverage and refine the line work so the lower half holds detail instead of filling in.

designs.title: Cape Agulhas Lighthouse
designs.why: Cleanest headline (the arch clears everything) and the banded tower translates well to one ink, giving a clear focal point at 3 m. The fact block is sparse but readable. Still let down by traced linework on the buildings and a fynbos foreground so dense it becomes a dark slab across the hem of the frame.
designs.fix: Lighten and simplify the fynbos foreground, using open hatching instead of solid fill, so the tower and banding dominate and the print weighs less on the shirt.

designs.title: Phare de Saint-Mathieu
designs.why: Strongest story: the abbey ruin beside the tower is distinctive, and the PHARE DE / SAINT-MATHIEU / place-line stack has good typographic rhythm. The drawing is the roughest of the four, though: bubbly outlines on the abbey stonework and tower, and the same heavy, near-solid cliff mass at the bottom. The two-line heading pushes the tower and fact column down, which leaves the top half tight.
designs.fix: Rework the abbey and tower line art with crisp engraved strokes in place of the auto-traced blobs, and cut ink density in the lower cliffs.
